subject: Proportions for TV units and feature walls
hook: Lift the TV unit off the floor and the whole wall looks wider.
ig:
Lift the TV unit off the floor and the whole wall looks wider.

A floating base is one of the simplest proportion tricks on a media wall. Here's why it works:

The floor keeps going. When you can see flooring underneath, your eye doesn't stop at a plinth, so the room reads larger.

The unit looks lighter. A long, low console hovering off the floor feels less bulky than the same unit sat on a plinth, which matters in smaller living rooms.

Cleaning is easier. A hoover head goes straight underneath; no dusty kick line.

Cables stay hidden. The back of the unit can carry grommets and a cable route up to the screen, so nothing dangles.

The catch: it has to be fixed properly into the wall behind, so we check what the wall is made of at survey stage and plan the fixings to suit.

Which detail matters most in your living room: storage, hidden cables or a lighter look? DM us and tell us about the space.
fb:
A small detail with a big effect: floating the TV unit.

With the floor carrying on underneath, the room looks bigger and the unit looks lighter. It's easier to clean under, and the cables can be routed through the back so nothing trails down to the sockets.

It does need fixing properly into the wall, which is why we check the wall construction when we survey. Have a look at our TV units and send us a message if you'd like one designed for your room.
